newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves Bowland's $18.1 mln gold venture.
newsitem.headline: China approves Bowland's $18.1 mln gold venture.

text.p: China's State Planning Commission has authorised the Bowland Mines and Resources Co of Canada to form a gold joint venture, officials said on Tuesday.
"The proposed joint venture has been approved," a State Planning Commission official said in Beijing.

Total investment in the venture, the Guangxi Baise Bowland Gold Mines Co in the Baise area of southern China's Guangxi region, will reach $18.1 million, an official of the new company said by telephone from Baise.
Of the total, Bowland would invest $4.5 million and the Guangxi Gold Co would invest $13.6 million, he said.
China decided to open low-grade gold mines to foreign investors on a trial basis in August 1993 and last May agreed to let foreign firms conduct risk-prospecting in selected areas.

The new project, with proven reserves of 11.5 tonnes, is expected to produce 0.9849 tonnes of gold annually when in full operation. All of its gold would be sold to the People's Bank of China, the central bank, he said without elaborating.
